articles.title: "No entiendo la gestión física que se está haciendo de Rodri"
articles.standfirst: David Bernabéu cuestiona el reparto de minutos de Flick, advierte del riesgo de llegar a abril con los jugadores "quemados" y apunta a una posible salida de Balde en invierno
articles.summary: David Bernabéu cuestiona el reparto de minutos de Flick, advierte del riesgo de llegar a abril con los jugadores "quemados" y apunta a una posible salida de Balde en invierno
articles.body: David Bernabéu puso el foco en la gestión de Hansi Flick con Rodri durante su intervención en Radio MARCA. Las molestias en el gemelo que obligaron al centrocampista a retirarse en el descanso ante el Aston Villa reabrieron un debate que el periodista ya había planteado tras su suplencia contra el PSG, cómo administra el técnico los esfuerzos de una de sus piezas fundamentales. "Sinceramente, no entiendo la gestión física que se está haciendo de Rodri", afirmó Bernabéu. Su crítica se centra en la acumulación de minutos del internacional y en los escasos descansos que, a su juicio, ha tenido en encuentros que el Barcelona ya había encarrilado. "Rodri ha venido para jugar partidos grandes esta temporada. El día del PSG no es titular", recordó. Según explicó, el centrocampista llegaba a aquella cita después de ocho titularidades consecutivas y, sin embargo, solo participó en los últimos 25 minutos. Bernabéu también señaló lo sucedido frente al Alavés como ejemplo de una gestión mejorable: "Viene de jugar 90 minutos ante el Alavés, que vas ganando 4-0 en el descanso". Para el periodista, ese tipo de escenarios deberían permitir a Flick repartir esfuerzos y preservar a sus futbolistas.

articles.title: El desconocido demócrata que ha puesto contra las cuerdas a Donald Trump
articles.standfirst: Jon Ossoff ha sido reelegido como senador en Georgia y, según ha podido saber Oddschecker, su figura se ha disparado en las apuestas de cara a las elecciones de 2028 en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: Jon Ossoff ha sido reelegido como senador en Georgia y, según ha podido saber Oddschecker, su figura se ha disparado en las apuestas de cara a las elecciones de 2028 en Estados Unidos
articles.body: Las elecciones de medio mandato han supuesto un importante revés electoral para Donald Trump y han agitado el panorama político estadounidense de cara a las presidenciales de 2028. El presidente afronta ahora dos años con un Congreso y un Senado bajo control demócrata. Un escenario que condicionará buena parte de sus decisiones hasta el final de la legislatura. Además, los resultados han impulsado a nuevos nombres dentro de la oposición y han provocado movimientos en los mercados de apuestas sobre quién ocupará la Casa Blanca dentro de dos años. La jornada del pasado martes, 3 de noviembre, terminó con una victoria demócrata en ambas cámaras. Un resultado que permitirá al partido opositor ejercer un mayor control sobre la agenda legislativa y la supervisión de la Administración Trump. Las elecciones de medio mandato han servido así para tomar la temperatura al clima político del país y dibujar un escenario más complicado para el presidente republicano. Ese cambio de escenario también se refleja en las cuotas de las apuestas a las elecciones presidenciales de Estados Unidos. Según los datos facilitados de Codere, la posibilidad de que Donald Trump vuelva a ser elegido presidente en 2028 ha alcanzado una cotización de 40.00. En el mercado de candidatos, el nombre que aparece mejor situado es el de JD Vance, con una cuota de 4.5 en Codere y William Hill. Sin embargo, hay otro aspirante demócrata que ha comenzado a ganar protagonismo y cuya presencia en las apuestas ha crecido con fuerza durante las últimas horas: Jon Ossoff. Su nombre también figura con una cuota de 4.5 en Bet365; Betfair y William Hill. Con apenas 39 años, Ossoff acaba de conseguir la reelección como senador por Georgia después de imponerse al republicano Mike Collins, respaldado por Trump. Su victoria permite a los demócratas conservar un escaño clave y refuerza la proyección nacional de un político al que ya se señala como posible aspirante presidencial en 2028. Las apuestas han empezado a recoger ese movimiento: según ha podido saber Oddschecker, el volumen de apuestas en torno a su figura se ha incrementado un 17% después de conservar su puesto en el Senado. Un cifra superior a la del propio JD Vance (11%), Newsom (16%) u Ocasio-Cortez (9%) Las mejores casas de apuestas seguirán pendientes de la evolución de Ossoff, que ha pasado de ser una figura relativamente poco conocida fuera de Georgia a aparecer en las quinielas de la carrera presidencial. Todavía queda mucho camino hasta las elecciones de 2028 y el escenario puede cambiar considerablemente. Pero su victoria en un estado decisivo para la política estadounidense le ha situado bajo los focos. Trump ya conoce a uno de los nombres que podría tener enfrente si decide buscar un segundo mandato.

articles.title: Como Breaks Bayern Munich’s Champions League Record With 9 Goals vs. Lens
articles.summary: Como became the first away team to score nine goals in a Champions League match with a 9-1 rout at Lens on Wednesday.
articles.body: Como became the first away team to score nine goals in a Champions League match with a 9-1 rout at Lens on Wednesday. Cesc Fabregas’ team made it three victories in four matches of its debut season in the competition and moved up to fourth in the league phase standings. "Today everything went our way," Fabregas said. "A great night for Como and our fans." The previous best scoring performance by an away club was Bayern Munich’s 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020. It matched the biggest margin of victory after Liverpool and Real Madrid’s 8-0 home victories against Besiktas and Malmo, respectively. Tasos Douvikas had a hat trick and has now scored in all four of Como’s matches. He leads the Champions League with six goals. Nico Paz also found the net and then instead of celebrating went and grabbed a T-shirt featuring an image of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife forward who died following an on-field collision with the opposing team’s goalkeeper. Paz spent time in Tenerife’s youth system from 2014-16. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli also scored for Como. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como’s youth team and hasn’t even played in Serie A yet. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham Scores Brilliant Back Heel Goal For Real Madrid In Comeback Win
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho hailed "extraordinary" Jude Bellingham after the midfielder scored a brilliant back-heeled goal against AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday.
articles.body: Jose Mourinho hailed "extraordinary" Jude Bellingham after the midfielder scored a brilliant back-heeled goal against AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday. On a night when Bellingham became the youngest player to make 60 appearances in European club soccer's top competition, the England midfielder scored and was named player of the match as Madrid rallied to a 3-2 win. "He is a unique player. Today, there is no midfielder in world football like Jude, who is complete on all levels," Mourinho said via translation. "I don’t have many words because, for me, he is an absolutely extraordinary player. Even on a day when he doesn’t have a great match, one of those jaw-dropping performances, he still brings work, leadership, ambition, quality, and goal-scoring ability. He is an extraordinary player." Bellingham, who was also the youngest player to make 50 appearances, reached his latest landmark at the age of 23 years, 128 days, overtaking iconic former Madrid goalkeeper Iker Casillas. He struck in the 32nd minute by connecting with Marc Cucurella’s cross and flicking a first-time shot past goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli. "It was just instinct really," he said. "I found myself in a good position and managed to do the only thing that came naturally in that position. It was a nice one." Madrid twice fought back from a goal down before Federico Valverde struck a stoppage time winner. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Guinness World Record broken as 53 red cards shown in Brazil under-20 match
articles.summary: Mass brawl at Uberlandia vs Mamore results in 43 cards for players, eight for coaching staff and two for board members.
articles.body:
An under-20 football match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais has descended into chaos as the referee hands out a record 53 red cards after an enormous brawl.

The brawl took place during the first leg of a state championship semifinal match between Uberlandia and Mamore on Sunday.

In his report of the match, referee Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto said the trouble began early in the second half when a number of Uberlandia officials invaded the field of play after one of their players was sent off.

The match was halted for 40 minutes and eventually restarted with Mamore going on to score in the ninth minute of stoppage time to take a 3-1 lead.

According to reports in Brazilian media, Mamore player Davi taunted Uberlandia players during the goal celebrations, which sparked the brawl that led to the deluge of red cards.

A total of 43 players and eight members of the coaching staff were sent off while two Uberlandia board members were also dismissed.

“In the 54th minute of the second half, a generalised brawl broke out, making it impossible to show the red cards and to carry out the match-closing protocol,” Drosghic Modesto wrote in his report.

“Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared the match ended.”

Drosghic Modesto added that a police report was filed over threats made against the referee and Mamore’s team vandalised the dressing room after the match.

The previous Guinness World Record for the most red cards shown in a match was 36, which occurred in February 2011 during a fifth-division match in Argentina between Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas.

On Wednesday, Uberlandia said it would be forfeiting the second leg of the semifinal in a “gesture of fair play” because Mamore did not have enough eligible players to field a team.

The forfeit saw Mamore qualify for the final of the tournament.

“The club has also not remained silent: The appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally because athletic development is, above all, a matter of personal development,” Uberlandia added.

articles.title: La DGT toma esta medida para evitar unas distracciones que el año pasado dejaron 546 fallecidos
articles.standfirst: Se trata de una nueva campaña con la que trata de combatir las distracciones al volante, que el año pasado dejaron 546 fallecidos en España
articles.summary: Se trata de una nueva campaña con la que trata de combatir las distracciones al volante, que el año pasado dejaron 546 fallecidos en España
articles.body: Hay accidentes de los que uno se pregunta cómo pudieron suceder. En ellos no se ha dado un adelantamiento peligroso, un choque por alcance ni una maniobra inesperada de otro conductor. Tan solo interviene un coche que se sale poco a poco de la carretera o sigue recto cuando debería tomar una curva. A veces basta una simple mirada al móvil por parte del conductor para que esto suceda. Fruto de esta preocupación, la DGT ha decidido lanzar una nueva campaña de concienciación bajo un mensaje muy directo: "Si conduces, solo conduce". Su sencillez recuerda en gran medida a aquel "Si bebes, no conduzcas" que popularizó el cantante Stevie Wonder en 1985, aunque en esta ocasión ninguna estrella pone rostro ni voz al anuncio. Y en una de sus imágenes, en las que se ve una mano asomada por la ventanilla, está inspirada en aquella de "¿Te gusta conducir?", de BMW. Estará presente en televisión, radio, medios digitales, redes sociales, cines y publicidad exterior hasta el 13 de diciembre. Todo para recordarnos que apartar la atención de la carretera, aunque sea durante unos segundos, puede tener consecuencias fatales. Hay que recordar que el pasado año fueron 546 las personas que perdieron la vida en nuestras carreteras interurbanas por salidas de vía, mientras que cerca de 1.800 sufrieron heridas de gravedad. De hecho, este tipo de siniestro fue el responsable del 43% de los fallecimientos en carretera. Las distracciones (sobre todo por el móvil), la velocidad inadecuada y, en menor medida, el sueño, están detrás de la mayor parte de estos accidentes. De hecho, aparecen como causa en tres de cada cuatro salidas de vía. Además, se ha podido constatar que en nueve de cada diez salidas de vía no interviene ningún otro vehículo. Y en dos de cada tres casos, el conductor es la única persona implicada y no se aprecian señales de reacción (marcas de suelo por frenadas o derrapes, por ejemplo) antes del impacto. Si miramos los datos de 2025, el 72% de las salidas de vía mortales tuvo lugar en carreteras convencionales. Sobre todo en tramos de curvas, donde se concentró el 44% de los siniestros, con un balance de 243 personas fallecidas. En cuanto al momento del día, el 60% de los accidentes mortales se produjo entre las 8 y las 20 horas, frente al 40% que tuvo lugar en horario nocturno. Por perfil de las víctimas, el 83% eran hombres y uno de cada tres tenía entre 45 y 64 años. La DGT siempre nos recuerda que los sistemas de asistencia a la conducción, como los avisos de distracción o las alertas de somnolencia, pueden ayudar a reducir el número de accidentes, pero no sustituyen la necesidad de que estemos atentos a la carretera.

articles.title: Argentina no es mejor, es favorita
articles.summary: La opinión de Alberto Bote.
articles.body: Argentina es favorita. Sin paliativos. Sí, quizá no es mejor que España, algunas de sus grandes estrellas no llegan en el mejor momento y puesto por puesto, el ranking es ligeramente español. Pero lo ocurrido en 2022 y 2024 pesa y mucho. Y la camiseta, ese intangible tan presente en esta competición, ni que decir tiene. Porque el combinado de Gaby Reca y Rodri Ovide se ha ganado el mérito del favoritismo en base a las victorias de Dubai y Doha donde, por cierto, no contaban con viento a favor y supieron hacer que todo cuadrara para definir en la agonía o la épica. Escenarios diferentes, nombres distintos y un mismo resultado, la albiceleste campeonando en el tercer punto. Una realidad en la que Argentina se mueve bien. Especialistas en tirar la presión fuera, en trasladarla al rival para dibujar un escenario donde la responsabilidad es para los de Juanjo Gutiérrez, el combinado albiceleste seleccionado para la cita mundialista sabe jugar ese otro pádel, el del relato, que en la previa a la final les permite tener un plus que les haga creer, aún más, que pueden repetir hazaña alejando la 'mufa'. El argentino, cuando se pone la camiseta de la selección, adquiere un sentimiento nacionalista, de hermanamiento, orgullo y representación que genera envidia, incluso, en algunas estrellas rivales. Lo hemos visto en otros deportes y en el pádel no podía ser de otra forma. Y claro que tiene un efecto directo. No va a hacer que una pelota entre o no, que el punto que lo cambia todo caiga del lado correcto, pero define un marco anímico y mental que motiva a que los jugadores que se ponen la camiseta albiceleste entren con un extra, casi en trance. ¿Alguien ha olvidado la exhibición de Libaak cuando era casi un desconocido con 19 años? ¿Y la actuación de Sanyo y Bela caída la noche dos años antes? Si hablamos de saber competir, los argentinos no tienen comparación. En el golpe a golpe, en la matemática, España cuenta con jugadores mejor posicionados. Siete de los 20 primeros rankeados son españoles por los seis de Argentina; si miramos los resultados del año, obviando que las tres primeras parejas tienen un componente de cada selección, los segundos espadas españoles marcan una pequeña diferencia de rendimiento; y la baja de última hora de Galán lo condiciona todo. Ni que decir tiene que Tapia, Chingotto o Augsburger pueden mirar de tú a tú a cualquier estrella española. Pequeños detalles que son insuficientes para decir que España es favorita, pero varios de ellos de peso para reconocer que tiene más combinaciones, más presión por ganar y, por qué no decirlo, hacen que sobre el papel sea mejor. La final se presuponía favorable para España hasta la confirmación de la ausencia de Galán y ese es un caldo de cultivo que se ha instalado en el pádel desde hace ya meses y que beneficia a Argentina. No recuerdo una edición así, y he cubierto ya unos cuantos mundiales de pádel, en la que se hable, elucubre y fantaseé tanto con cuál será la alineación de cada selección, en qué orden jugarán los primeros espadas y quién debe enfrentarse con quién. Un ambiente que enriquece el pádel y demuestra su crecimiento en interés y expectación. El hype por la final de la cita mundialista es altísimo y definida ya la carrera por el número uno entre los Golden Boys y Chingalán el título mundial de la FIP parece adquirir un valor extra que quizá, incluso, antes no tenía. La final del Mundial se presenta como la cita con mayúsculas del año. ¿Qué ocurrirá? Creo que nadie lo tiene claro a ciencia cierta, pero aunque solo lo confiesen en los círculos más cercanos, hasta las grandes estrellas de la pala coinciden en que España es (o era) superior y tiene más posibilidades para combinar, pero que Argentina, cuando se pone la albiceleste en el pádel, es Argentina con mayúsculas. Y sí, es la favorita.

articles.title: Una barandilla, una cascada, un atropello y un accidente: la historia de cuatro lesionados medulares en 'Backbone'
articles.standfirst: El documental de Red Bull recoge los testimonios de Sam Bloom, Delia Guggenheim, Thibaud Coudriou y Nico Langmann
articles.summary: El documental de Red Bull recoge los testimonios de Sam Bloom, Delia Guggenheim, Thibaud Coudriou y Nico Langmann
articles.body: Unas vacaciones en familia, un entrenamiento en bicicleta, un chapuzón en una cascada, un viaje en coche... Estas fueron las circunstancias en las que Sam Bloom, Delia Guggenheim, Thibaud Coudriou y Nico Langmann sufrieron una lesión medular que les cambió la vida y la transformó para siempre. Cuatro historias inspiradoras que recoge Red Bull en el docmunetal BACKBONE, un documental que cuenta con la leyenda del esquí Lindsey Vonn como la narradora. A través de su voz conecta las cuatro historias personales y explica la ciencia que hay detrás de las lesiones medulares y por qué la investigación es importante. En su intervención inicial, describe lo que significa no poder levantarse sin ayuda y vivir con dolor y limitaciones tras una lesión; sin embargo, distingue explícitamente su experiencia, que duró unos meses, de los cambios duraderos a los que se enfrentan los protagonistas del documental. Sam Bloom, que es tetracampeona mundial de surf adaptado, sufrió una lesión medular en 2013 cuando la barandilla de una azotea cedió durante unas vacaciones familiares en Tailandia. Una caída de seis metros en la que no sólo destrozó su espalda, sino su vida tal y como la conocía hasta entonces. La enfermera, cuyo marido y tres hijos fueron testigos del accidente, quedó paralizada del pecho para abajo. Pasó siete meses de rehabilitación y al regresar a casa tuvo que enfrentarse a una nueva realidad que no quería aceptar. “La odiaba demasiado como para aceptarla”, reconoció en su momento. Tuvo pensamientos oscuros, pero decidió aguantar por sus tres hijos y su marido. Cuidar de Penguin, una cría de urraca herida, proporcionó a la familia un objetivo común. De hecho, se rodó una película basándose en su historia: 'Penguin Bloom' (en España se tradujo como La Familia Bloom), en la que Naomi Watts se convertía en la pantalla en Sam. La actriz australiana también colabora. El kayak le ayudó a reconectar con la naturaleza. Después, una carta de Nola Wilson, madre del surfista profesional Julian Wilson y antigua surfista, animó a Bloom a volver al surf. Era el deporte que practicó durante su adolescencia en las playas de Sídney. El documental muestra el dolor persistente, la ayuda necesaria para meterse en el agua y la importancia de contar con una comunidad de compañeros de competición. "Espero que BACKBONE haga que la gente se pare a reflexionar y afronte de verdad la magnitud de lo que una lesión medular le arrebata a una persona. No solo la capacidad física para moverse, sino también la independencia, la identidad, el control y, a menudo, la vida que imaginabas que habrías tenido. Le puede pasar a cualquiera, en una fracción de segundo, y a veces sin que sea culpa tuya", reconoce Bloom. Hace dos años, Delia Guggenheim corrió un ultramaratón por el Sáhara. Tenía 21 años. En la primavera de 2025 estaba entrenando en bicicleta, estaba ya a cinco minutos de su casa, tras haber completado 100 kilómetros alrededor del lago de Zúrich, cuando un coche se aproximó por detrás a 80 km/h. La conductora estaba mirando su teléfono móvil y se la llevó por delante. Delia salió despedida sobre el capó y contra el parabrisas. Estaba consciente mientras yacía en el asfalto, pero ya no sentía las piernas. Ya en el lugar del accidente, le dijo a su madre: "Iré a los Juegos Paralímpicos". "Una lesión medular es mucho más que no poder caminar. Afecta a todo el cuerpo y cambia la vida cotidiana de formas en las que la mayoría de la gente ni siquiera piensa. Pero tú no eres tu lesión: no es ni una tragedia ni una historia de héroes, sino una vida con planes, ambición, sentido del humor y una buena dosis de sarcasmo. Lo único que queremos es que nos traten como a cualquier otra persona. Y el apoyo de las personas que te rodean marca la diferencia", dice. En BACKBONE, regresa al lugar del accidente y ve las imágenes de la colisión por primera vez. Recuerda cómo le costaba respirar, temiendo no sobrevivir, y cómo no podía hablar mientras estaba intubada. Se preparó en los Alpes para volver a participar en una carrera en el desierto del Sáhara en silla de ruedas. Y la ha completado. Un chapuzón en una cascada durante una excursión con amigos por el Gran Cañón de Arizona dejó a Thibaud Coudriou con una lesión en las vértebras cervicales, movilidad limitada en los brazos y sin movilidad en las manos. Se golpeó la cabeza contra el fondo y tuvo que ser trasladado en helicóptero a un hospital. En cuestión de segundos, la vida del francés cambió para siempre. Fue trasladado de urgencia a Utah y luego al Hospital Craig en Denver, uno de los hospitales más prestigiosos del mundo para el tratamiento de lesiones. El documental recoge su relato y el de los amigos que le ayudaron a rescatarlo, y luego sigue su rehabilitación en Nebraska, donde se enfrenta al dolor, la culpa, la incertidumbre y la necesidad de asistencia diaria. Antes de su lesión, había recorrido en bicicleta 30 países y completado un Ironman en menos de diez horas. La fisioterapia, aprender a desplazarse y establecer una rutina le ayudan a recuperar el contacto con el movimiento; las escenas posteriores le muestran explorando la naturaleza con una bicicleta de mano, un «trail hopper» y una silla de ruedas manual. Nico Langmann tenía dos años cuando un accidente de coche le aplastó la columna vertebral. Su infancia estuvo marcada por la determinación de su familia de que volviera a caminar, lo que incluyó años de terapias alternativas en países como la India y Rusia. Describe la presión que suponían esas expectativas y recuerda que, a veces, fingía que los tratamientos funcionaban para hacer felices a sus padres. En su adolescencia, decidió dejar de perseguirlas y aceptar su vida tal y como era. El tenis en silla de ruedas pasó a ser fundamental para su futuro: se proclamó campeón mundial juvenil, ganó torneos internacionales y representó a Austria en los Juegos Paralímpicos. Su ambición de competir en un Grand Slam demuestra que la aceptación no es el final de las aspiraciones, sino la base para sus propios objetivos.

articles.title: NHL Trade Rumor: Philadelphia Flyers could absorb Yakov Trenin’s contract to help Minnesota Wild land Dylan Larkin from Detroit
articles.summary: Explore how the Philadelphia Flyers could play a crucial role in a potential trade involving Dylan Larkin, aiding the Minnesota Wild while absorbing Yakov Trenin’s contract. Discover the implications, expected compensation, and how this trade could benefit all teams involved.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Flyers have reportedly emerged as a potential third-team facilitator in trade discussions involving Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin and the Minnesota Wild. Flyers general manager Daniel Brière could reportedly help the deal move forward by taking on Wild forward Yakov Trenin’s $3.5 million contract.The proposed arrangement could give Minnesota a route to acquire its targeted center while allowing Detroit to pursue a stronger return. However, the reported framework remains speculative, and no agreement has been confirmed by the three organizations.Philadelphia Flyers enter Dylan Larkin NHL trade talks involving Minnesota WildThe Philadelphia Flyers could help facilitate a potential three-team NHL trade involving Dylan Larkin, the Detroit Red Wings, and the Minnesota Wild. According to Daily Faceoff's Anthony Di Marco, Philadelphia may be willing to take on Yakov Trenin’s contract despite not being among Larkin’s preferred destinations.Flyers general manager Daniel Brière reportedly recognizes that acquiring Larkin directly is unlikely because the Detroit captain has not included Philadelphia on his 10-team trade list. Rather than pursuing the center, Brière could potentially help another organization complete the transaction.The reported proposal involves Philadelphia absorbing Trenin’s $3.5 million contract from Minnesota. However, the Flyers would reportedly expect meaningful compensation before agreeing to take on the financial commitment.One reported framework involves young Minnesota Wild center prospect Charlie Stramel and a future first-round draft pick being part of a potential package for Philadelphia winger Owen Tippett.Such an arrangement could give the Flyers additional future assets while helping Minnesota create the financial and roster flexibility needed to pursue Larkin. The exact structure and whether Tippett would actually be moved remain unconfirmed.How could the three-team Dylan Larkin trade benefit everyone?A three-way trade would allow Detroit, Minnesota and Philadelphia to address separate roster needs in one transaction. Minnesota would get the top-line center it wants, Detroit would get an established NHL player and some additional assets, and Philadelphia would add to its collection of prospects and draft picks.The Minnesota Wild have apparently been pursuing Larkin for months. Detroit’s captain would provide an experienced center who could contribute offensively and provide leadership to Minnesota’s forward group.His potential arrival would give the Wild another proven offensive option and add depth to the team’s center. But Minnesota would have to make a package that is acceptable, given the contract and roster implications.Why might Detroit Red Wings consider the proposal?Detroit could potentially use a multi-team framework to secure a more attractive return than a straightforward one-for-one arrangement. Receiving an impact NHL player and additional assets could help the Red Wings address multiple roster needs if they decide to move their captain.Montreal Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes has also reportedly remained interested, although Larkin would need to include Montreal among his approved destinations for that possibility to advance.For now, the Flyers' reported involvement adds another layer to the developing NHL trade rumors. The proposed framework could offer a path forward, but Larkin’s trade list, contract considerations and the assets Detroit is asking for are still major factors. articles.title: “Challenging circumstances involving my family”: Connor Hellebuyck’s Winnipeg Jets trade request ahead of his NHL return with New Jersey Devils
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck has opened up about the difficult family circumstances that led to his trade request from the Winnipeg Jets, as he prepares to face his former team with the New Jersey Devils. Read more about his heartfelt letter to Jets fans and what to expect on his return to Winnipeg.
articles.body: Connor Hellebuyck has revealed that difficult family circumstances played a significant role in his decision to request a trade from the Winnipeg Jets. In an open letter to Jets fans, the former goaltender thanked the organization and Winnipeg community while explaining why he and his family believed a fresh start was necessary.The revelation comes ahead of Hellebuyck’s first return to Winnipeg as a member of the New Jersey Devils. He also asked fans to respect his family’s privacy, making clear that he does not intend to disclose further personal details. Hellebuyck explains Winnipeg Jets departure ahead of Devils NHL reunionHellebuyck said family circumstances were among the major considerations behind his decision to leave Winnipeg. He explained that the choice followed extensive thought and discussions with his family, who ultimately agreed that moving elsewhere was the best option.In his Instagram letter, Hellebuyck acknowledged that his trade request had disappointed supporters who had followed his career in Manitoba. He wrote:“I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career.”He then directly addressed the personal circumstances behind his decision, stating:“There were several considerations that went into my decision, including some very challenging circumstances involving my family.”The 33-year-old goaltender did not provide specific details about those circumstances. Instead, he asked fans to respect his family’s privacy and explained that the decision came after careful consideration.Why did Connor Hellebuyck express gratitude toward Winnipeg?Hellebuyck said his time in Winnipeg meant a lot to him, despite the difficult circumstances surrounding his departure, and reflected on establishing a life in Manitoba, raising his family there and enjoying the outdoor activities of the province; particularly fishing.Hellebuyck concluded his message with a heartfelt acknowledgment of the city, writing:“I'll never forget the pride I felt representing Winnipeg, and I wish the Jets and the entire community nothing but the best.”How did Connor Hellebuyck’s Winnipeg Jets departure unfold?Hellebuyck’s exit from the Winnipeg Jets was complicated by a training camp holdout as he sought a trade. The situation resulted in a suspension covering the first three weeks of the regular season before Winnipeg eventually dealt him to the New Jersey Devils on October 23, 2026.The reported trade package included prospect Alexander Command, forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, goaltender Nico Daws, a 2027 seventh-round selection, and a 2029 second-round pick.What can fans expect from Hellebuyck’s return to Winnipeg?Hellebuyck will play his old team in Winnipeg on Nov. 10, 2026, his first game in the city as a member of the New Jersey Devils. His departure was under somewhat controversial circumstances and he recently sent a message to Jets fans that is sure to draw attention to the reunion.Fans in Winnipeg will get to see a former foundation of the franchise return, but in a different color. Hellebuyck’s letter could also shed some light on a decision that left some questions about his exit.So the next game is about more than the standings in the NHL standings or the score of the game. It will mark the return of a goaltender who spent years representing Winnipeg and has now explained why leaving the organization became the right choice for his family.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Four candidates, including Sardar Singh, dropped from IOA SOM election race; 23 remain in fray
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Sardar Singh, B Sumeeth Reddy, Om Prakash Singh Karhana and Sunith Singh have failed to make the final list of validly nominated candidates
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sardar Singh, B Sumeeth Reddy, Om Prakash Singh Karhana and Sunith Singh have failed to make the final list of validly nominated candidates ahead of November 9 elections for IOA's Sportspersons of Outstanding merit (SOM).Four candidates have not made the cut for the Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections following scrutiny of nominations, reducing the field from 27 draft nominees to 23.The final list of validly nominated candidates, issued by Electoral Officer Sanjay Kumar Srivastava on Thursday, features 12 men and 11 women. The draft list published on October 31 had 15 male and 12 female candidates.Former India hockey captain Sardar Singh, badminton player B Sumeeth Reddy and shot putter Om Prakash Singh Karhana are the three male candidates missing from the final list. Sunith Singh is the only female candidate from the draft list who has not made the cut.The remaining candidates include prominent sporting figures such as current IOA president PT Usha, vice-president Gagan Narang, Olympic medallists Vijender Singh and Yogeshwar Dutt, former Athletics Federation of India president Adille Sumariwalla, former table tennis player Achanta Sharath Kamal and badminton star Saina Nehwal.The final list follows the publication of the draft nominations on October 31 and the subsequent scrutiny process.How the SOM election process worksThe SOM elections are part of the wider IOA electoral process for the 2026-2030 term. The electoral college comprises 80 Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit, equally divided between 40 men and 40 women.The November 9 election will see these 80 members vote to elect eight representatives to the IOA General Assembly — four men and four women.The nomination process requires candidates to be proposed and seconded by members of the published SOM electoral roll. The election guidelines also prescribe restrictions on proposing and seconding multiple candidates in the same gender category. Digital signatures have been permitted, with voting to take place virtually.Following the scrutiny of nominations, candidates have November 6 and 7 to withdraw. The final list of contesting candidates is scheduled to be published on November 7, ahead of polling, counting and declaration of results on November 9.The eight elected SOM representatives will become part of the IOA General Assembly. Of these, one male and one female representative will subsequently be elected to the IOA Executive Council.Their participation will therefore extend beyond the SOM elections themselves, giving the elected athletes a direct role in the composition of the IOA's governing body for the next four-year term.IOA SOM Elections candidates:MALE1. articles.title: '14 to 114': PM Modi hails India's para-athletes after historic Asian Para Games medal haul, sets sights on 2028 LA Paralympics
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday hailed India's para-athletes for their record-breaking performance at the 2026 Asian Para Games,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday hailed India's para-athletes for their record-breaking performance at the 2026 Asian Para Games, describing their achievements and struggles as an inspiration for the entire country, while urging them to turn their historic success into a launch pad for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics.Interacting with the medal winners at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex, Modi congratulated the contingent for its best-ever campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Games in Japan. India finished fourth in the overall standings with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — won by 97 para-athletes."Your magnificent performance shows that India is emerging as a great power in the world of sports. You have not only won medals, but you have also won the hearts of millions of Indians," Modi said."Your struggles and your achievements inspire every Indian. Earlier, parents were scared of supporting their kids in sporting careers. People would say nothing can be done about this system which did not support talent but just as you did not give up, we also stayed focussed on our goals," he added.Double gold medallists, including armless archer Sheetal Devi and visually impaired sprinter Simran, attended the interaction. The athletes presented gifts to the Prime Minister, who was also seen feeding sweets to some of them. Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse were present at the event.'14 to 114': Modi highlights India's rise in para-sportsModi underlined the scale of India's progress by recalling that the country had won just 14 medals, including one gold, at the 2010 edition. The latest haul also featured five world records, nine Asian records and podium sweeps by Indian athletes in four events.In a post on X, Modi highlighted India's remarkable rise from 14 medals at the 2010 edition to 114 in 2026, calling it a reflection of the immense talent and potential of the country's para-athletes. He also pointed to the campaign's five world records, nine Asian records and four podium sweeps, besides noting that 36 of the 61 debutants returned with medals.The Prime Minister also underlined the contribution of women, with 34 of the 56 female athletes winning medals. "Our athletes have shown that no dream is too big and no challenge too great when there is determination," he wrote, adding that India now stands firmly behind youngsters aspiring to pursue sports: "Now, if you have the talent, India will support you and cheer for you. Come, play and shine!"The Prime Minister also praised India's growing competitiveness across disciplines such as archery, athletics, shooting, swimming, table tennis, badminton, judo and powerlifting. He pointed out that 61 members of the contingent were making their Asian Para Games debut.Modi made special mention of javelin thrower Rinku Hooda, who dedicated his gold medal to his mother, who had died a couple of months before the Games. Rinku had lost his left arm in an accident as a young boy."You made the entire country emotional at that moment," Modi told him.LA 2028 next target for India's para-athletesModi also spoke about efforts to strengthen India's sporting ecosystem, including a sports goods manufacturing scheme worth more than Rs 1,800 crore, and urged athletes to set their sights on the next Paralympics."You should use this success as a launch pad for bigger goals. The next goal of India and most of you is Los Angeles 2028. Our goal is to have as many Indian players in LA 2028 as possible and win as many medals as possible. Celebrate this moment and start preparing for the future," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patriots QB Drake Maye Talks Impact Of 'Legend' Tom Brady Calling Week 9 Game
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye expressed what it means to have franchise icon Tom Brady call their Week 9 game.
articles.body: Tom Brady is going home — for the weekend. Brady has been an NFL color commentator for 49 combined regular season and postseason games on FOX, but this Sunday, the NFL's all-time passing leader will call his first New England Patriots game, as New England hosts the Green Bay Packers in an AFC vs. NFC matchup between two 5-3 teams (4:25 p.m. ET on FOX). "It's obviously cool," Patriots quarterback Drake Maye said in a press conference on Wednesday afternoon about Brady, who started 19 seasons and was present for 20 seasons altogether in New England (2000-19), calling the Patriots' Week 9 game. "What a legend to come back here, and it's definitely cool for him, I bet, to come back and call a game in the stadium where he won so many games and was elite in this stadium, and really part of him, the fans, and their teams built Gillette into what it is now, so I bet it's cool for him. "I know he hangs around the field sometimes, so just try to go appreciate him for what he left here." Of course, Brady, who's first in franchise history with 74,571 passing yards, 541 passing touchdowns and 219 regular-season wins, helped guide the Patriots to each of their six Super Bowl triumphs: 2001, 2003, 2004, 2014, 2016 and 2018. Brady then spent the last three seasons of his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2020-22), highlighted by winning the Super Bowl in his first season with the team in 2020. Brady joined FOX as the network's lead NFL analyst in 2024, calling games with veteran play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt. As for the present, the Patriots have won four of their last five games, with Maye, the runner-up for the 2025 NFL MVP Award, getting off the mat following a slow start to the season. In the wake of throwing a combined six interceptions and posting a 58.6 passer rating through New England's first three games, Maye has since totaled 1,398 passing yards, 14 passing touchdowns, two interceptions and a 122.2 passer rating over the Patriots' last five games, while completing 68.8% of his passes. He has also rushed for 134 yards and three scores.

articles.title: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans has high praise for new WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.summary: Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans says Marvin Harrison Jr has been "attentive," "dialed in" and is "very well-versed in the playbook" after the bye week...
articles.body:
Since trading for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. back in mid-October, he has continued to get acclimated to the Houston Texans ' offense.

He only played 19 percent of the offensive snaps in his debut against the Jacksonville Jaguars , but had his first touchdown as a member of the Texans in their loss to the New York Giants .

"Marvin has done a great job," Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said. "Since the first day he's gotten here, when it comes to learning the playbook, Marvin's a really smart player. He's picked up on everything fairly quickly. He's been attentive. He's been dialed in, studying a lot. He's very well-versed in the playbook."

With the bye week, Harrison had additional time to familiarize himself with Houston's offense ahead of their game this Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. He actually played against the Chargers earlier this season with the Arizona Cardinals and had one reception for 33 yards. However, he should end up with more than one reception in this game.

During the loss to the Giants, second-year standout Jaylin Noel suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. Prior to his injury, he had been Houston's leading receiver. With that injury, Harrison should get more offensive snaps and chances to make plays.

With the chemistry he has with Houston's quarterback C.J. Stroud going back to college, Harrison could have a monster second half of the season with the Texans' offense, starting this Sunday on the road against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Mousinho gives updates on Portsmouth duo’s injuries
articles.summary: Portsmouth boss John Mousinho says Marko Milovanovic will miss Saturday’s game against Stoke City after suffering a quad injury in the win over Swansea.The s...
articles.body:
Portsmouth boss John Mousinho says Marko Milovanovic will miss Saturday's game against Stoke City after suffering a quad injury in the win over Swansea.

The striker was forced off in Tuesday's 3-1 victory and is due to undergo a scan to determine the extent of the issue.

"Marko is going to have a scan tomorrow so we will find out more," Mousinho told the Portsmouth News.

"I don't know how long he could be out. We won't see him this weekend and then we'll see how that settles down.

"It doesn't look great when a player pulls up like that but you never know.

"He was okay this morning but I think the scan will tell everything. It was his quad."

Iyad Mohamed was also forced off against Swansea, though Mousinho says his issue is not expected to be serious.

"Exactly the same," he said when asked whether Mohamed would also be assessed.

"I don't think Iyad's is anywhere near as severe as Marko's and so we'll see what the results are there."

articles.title: Brewers Lose Top Exec To A's Front Office
articles.summary: The A's have a new GM
articles.body:
Just one week after helping the Milwaukee Brewers win their first World Series title in franchise history, Cam Castro is already moving on.

On Wednesday, the A's announced Castro as their new general manager. He'll serve under their new president of baseball operations, Taylor Smith, who joined the team two weeks ago.

Castro, 36, joined the Brewers in 2019. He quickly worked his way up despite his young age, spending the last two seasons as their senior vice president of player development and performance.

After helping lead Milwaukee to the mountaintop, Castro will try to do he same with the A's, who are coming off five straight losing seasons and haven't won a championship since 1989. Fortunately for them, he's already used to working with limited resources and a tight budget.

articles.title: The Sabres’ Dylan Larkin Problem Isn’t the Assets
articles.summary: Buffalo has the assets for Dylan Larkin and has talked to Detroit, and a Sabres insider still isn't sold. #RedWings
articles.body:
Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin has been suspended without pay since Oct. 29 , when he told the team he no longer wanted to be part of the organization, and a Dylan Larkin trade is still stuck behind the market he has limited himself to. He has given the Red Wings a list of 10 teams he would accept a deal to, and the Buffalo Sabres are not one of them.

Why a Dylan Larkin trade to Buffalo is complicated

Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic , who covers the Sabres, took a fan mailbag question Wednesday about whether Buffalo could get into the Larkin market at all.

"But the Sabres are not on his expanded 10-team trade list. How much will that list have to expand before Buffalo ends up on it? Are the Sabres even a more attractive option than simply staying in Detroit? Yes, Buffalo ended its playoff drought, but that's still just one year. Assuming he doesn't want to go to a Canadian team, that leaves 26 teams.

"I wonder if the Sabres would get on the list if it got to 15 teams? Would it take 20? And how much more would the Sabres have to pay for the Red Wings to be compelled to move him within the division? All of those questions make me hesitant to get people too excited about the idea. I also think the Sabres should be wary about adding a player who essentially needs to be begged to come to Buffalo. You don't want to be someone's 15th choice when you're giving up the assets required to get a player like Larkin."

Larkin's camp has already said no to a longer list

Fairburn's question about how far the list would have to stretch already has an answer, and it is not an encouraging one for Buffalo. Larkin started with three teams and expanded to 10: the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. TSN hockey insider Pierre LeBrun reported Tuesday that Buffalo is one of the teams sitting off that list, along with Montreal, Boston and Los Angeles, and that Larkin's camp, led by agent Pat Brisson, has told the Red Wings no again in recent days.

That is the part of this that matters most to Sabres fans. Buffalo does not need Larkin to warm to the idea of Buffalo in general. It needs him to add the one team in his own division that would cost Detroit the most to do business with. Larkin is in the fourth season of an eight-year contract with an annual cap hit of $8.7 million, and he is forfeiting roughly $41,000 a day while the suspension runs. DSN has already covered why several teams that are on the list have hesitated .

Being in the same division makes things complicated

Would Detroit be willing to move Larkin inside its own division to a team like Buffalo? Probably not, and the standings explain why. Entering Thursday, Buffalo is 7-5-3 with 17 points and Detroit is 7-6-3 with 17 points , tied in the Atlantic Division with the Sabres holding a game in hand. These are two teams chasing the same playoff spot. If the Sabres and the Red Wings ever completed a trade involving Larkin, it would be a genuine surprise.

A Buffalo fan named Samuel D. asked , " Is it time to put the pipe dream trade ideas to rest for now? After losing the goalie trade, chatter has picked up around Dylan Larkin. I don't see this team making a move in the near future, so should the fans give up on this idea for now? "

Fairburn's answer gave Sabres general manager Jarmo Kekäläinen credit for doing the work, then took the air out of the idea anyway.

"Trades are fun, especially in a league where free agency has become even more watered down over the years. So I get why people want to throw ideas around and play general manager. And I do think it's fair to expect Kekäläinen to make a significant deal at some point this season. He's circled around a few doozies this calendar year between Colton Parayko and Connor Hellebuyck . That said, the idea of Larkin might be a non-starter.

"The Sabres have the assets to pull it off and have had conversations with the Red Wings about those assets. But Kekäläinen is the type to have those conversations about any big-name player who's available. He wouldn't be doing his job otherwise. Larkin would fill arguably their most glaring need for a No. 1 center and comes at a reasonable cap hit."

Buffalo still has a roster to sort out after missing on Hellebuyck, who was traded to the New Jersey Devils on Oct. 23 . Going after Larkin would be a move that fits the need. The problem is that he has not asked to go there, and the people who speak for him keep saying he does not plan to.

articles.title: Baltimore Ravens Turn to Jacoby Brissett After Losing Lamar Jackson and His Backup to Injuries
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are making a major change involving a quarterback as injuries continue to create problems for the team’s offense. Baltimore is finalizin...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are making a major change involving a quarterback as injuries continue to create problems for the team's offense.

Baltimore is finalizing a trade with the Arizona Cardinals to acquire veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett , according to an ESPN report published Wednesday, November 4. The trade is expected to be finalized this weekend.

The move comes after Ravens starting quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a serious thumb injury on November 1, requiring surgery, and could sideline him for the remainder of the season.

The same day, backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury, that is expected to keep him out for the season.

With both quarterbacks unavailable, Baltimore will turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano for Thursday, November 5, against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Brissett, 33, is expected to join the Ravens afterward and could make his debut against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, November 16.

Meanwhile, Brissett's departure follows a shake-up in Arizona's quarterback lineup.

The veteran started the Cardinals' first eight games this season before being benched during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory over the Dallas Cowboys .

Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur subsequently named Gardner Minshew II the team's new starter, with rookie Carson Beck serving as his backup.

Brissett was moved to the third-string position and requested a trade after learning about the decision, according to ESPN.

LaFleur, 39, addressed the pending move on Wednesday.

"Out of respect for the process and just working to get stuff finalized, I mean, I really don't have much of a comment on it, but we're going to let the process play out with that," he said, ESPN reported.

The Ravens, meanwhile, have lost three consecutive games , dropping their record to 4-4 and placing them last in the AFC North.

Brissett will also be working with a familiar face in Baltimore: Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork , who previously coached him with the Arizona Cardinals and Cleveland Browns .

The terms of the trade have not yet been announced.

articles.title: Sharks star Macklin Celebrini refuses to disclose message from players-only meeting
articles.summary: The San Jose Sharks held a players-only meeting after their disappointing 7-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday, looking to address their recent woe...
articles.body:
The San Jose Sharks held a players-only meeting after their disappointing 7-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday, looking to address their recent woes.

San Jose has now lost three consecutive games and four of its last five, dropping to a 7-9-1 record. The latest drubbing was especially disconcerting, as the Sharks found themselves thoroughly outmatched by their California rivals at Crypto.com Arena.

Los Angeles took control almost immediately, with Adrian Kempe scoring just 1:23 into the contest. Kempe struck again later in the opening period, while Quinton Byfield added a power-play goal to give Los Angeles a comfortable 3-0 advantage after 20 minutes.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Captain Macklin Celebrini momentarily gave San Jose some momentum by scoring his sixth goal of the season early in the second period. However, the Kings responded with two more goals in the frame, including Kempe's third of the night, before eventually coming away with the five-goal win.

Following the defeat, reporters asked Celebrini about the message shared during the players-only gathering, but he made it clear that the conversation would remain within the locker room, opting not to disclose what the players had discussed. However, he acknowledged that the group needs to improve, saying, "To a man, we need to be better."

Forward Kiefer Sherwood also pointed to a lack of connection among teammates on the ice. Meanwhile, head coach Ryan Warsofsky welcomed the players' decision to address their situation themselves, expressing appreciation for the leadership shown by those attempting to bring the group together.

The Sharks currently occupy sixth place in the Pacific Division, with only Los Angeles and Vancouver Canucks holding worse records in the division. San Jose also ranks 28th in the NHL in scoring, averaging 2.53 goals per game, while their 3.53 goals allowed per contest place them tied for 27th.

The Sharks are attempting to end a seven-year postseason drought after finishing last season with a 39-35-8 record, just four points behind the Kings for the Western Conference's second wild-card position.

Their immediate challenge will be two more road games against the Minnesota Wild on Friday night and Dallas Stars on Saturday.

articles.title: Week 9 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fantasy Quarterbacks
articles.summary: Welcome back, readers!
articles.body:
Welcome back, readers! I am happy to return for a second year as The Sporting Tribune's fantasy football analyst. If you are new here, my mission is to help fantasy managers with any dilemmas or questions they may have through the course of the season to ultimately win their leagues. For the next 17 weeks, I will produce weekly fantasy content that will go over the waiver wire, rankings, and Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns.

Being a fantasy manager often means having to make difficult roster decisions, but I aim to take some of the guesswork out of it with my Start 'Em and Sit 'Em column for every position. It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride" or "sit Tommy DeVito." Instead, I search for players that could be perceived as fringe that could propel your lineups for weekly wins.

As always, if you have any questions or don't see your players here, feel free to follow me on Twitter (X) – @JamesNewell96 and send me a message, where I typically respond in a timely manner.

Trevor Lawrence @ BAL (Projected FPTS – 19.8): It's very rare to see a quarterback score 19 fantasy points while completing just 10 passes, but it goes to show how efficient Lawrence has been this season. He has totaled 19 or more fantasy points in three consecutive outings and in five of his last seven games. He should be kept in starting lineups this week in a QB-friendly matchup against the Ravens, who've been shredded by Joe Burrow and Josh Allen in back-to-back contests. Baltimore's defense will likely get gassed because of the offense's hardships without Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The Ravens have also allowed the eighth-most fantasy points and passing yards to quarterbacks this season.

Matthew Stafford @ WSH (Projected FPTS – 18.8): Things haven't been easy for Stafford and the Rams' offense, who are trying to find ways to replace Davante Adams' production. Stafford had a rough go last Sunday, scoring 8.3 fantasy points against the Chargers. I do imagine the reigning MVP will get back on track in Week Nine with a matchup against the Commanders on deck. Washington's defense has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game and the eighth-most points per dropback to opposing quarterbacks. They've also surrendered 17 or more fantasy points to five QBs this season.

Jared Goff @ MIA (Projected FPTS – 20.0): Goff scored just nine fantasy points against a historically blitz-heavy Vikings defense in Week Eight. Now that he's over that hurdle, he can safely return to lineups. He has a solid matchup this week against the Dolphins, who've given up the second-most fantasy points per dropback and the fifth-most points per game to quarterbacks this season. Since Week Two, Miami's defense has allowed four opposing QBs to post 20 or more fantasy points. Goff, who has the second-best TD-to-INT ratio (15:1) and is averaging the sixth-most fantasy points per game, should have no issue finishing as one of the top QBs of the week.

Honorable Mentions: Patrick Mahomes vs. NYJ; Malik Willis vs. DET; Kirk Cousins @ SF; Dak Prescott @ IND; Kyler Murray @ BUF; J.J. McCarthy @ PHI; Caleb Williams vs. TB.

Jordan Love @ NE (Projected FPTS – 18.0): Love has been stellar over the past month and enters the week as the QB5 in fantasy. Despite scoring 20-plus points in three of his last four games, he has a tough matchup against the Patriots this week. New England's defense has played better at home than on the road, allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks at home, compared to three finishes of 14 or more points on the road. This is a game where you should expect the Packers to establish their running game with Josh Jacobs.

Bryce Young vs. DEN (Projected FPTS – 16.0): After a red-hot start to the season, Young has simmered down over his last two starts, scoring just 15.78 fantasy points. The decline of the Panthers' offensive line and Young nursing a knee injury are the probable explanations for his struggles. articles.summary: DANIA BEACH — Florida Panthers Brad Marchand and Sasha Barkov are both skating while recovering from injury with Marchand giving […]
articles.body:
DANIA BEACH — Florida Panthers Brad Marchand and Sasha Barkov are both skating while recovering from injury with Marchand giving an update on when he could be back in the lineup.

Speaking at the unveiling of the new jetBlue Panthers-themed livery at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International on Thursday morning, Marchand said he would be back "soon enough.''

Last week, coach Paul Maurice said Marchand would be out three more weeks after he sustained a left knee injury on Oct. 6 in Los Angeles.

"I can't say it's this month, but probably within five weeks, six weeks,'' Marchand said.

Marchand said he is actually happy to be out right now considering how he felt after getting hurt while being pulled down as he crashed the net against the Kings.

He had to be helped off the ice by Niko Mikkola and Brady Tkachuk and it did not look good.

Marchand is just happy he's coming back sometime in the near future.

"I've never been so happy to be out for this amount of time,'' Marchand said. "The injury could have been so much worse. I've never hurt my knee before; I didn't know what to think when I went down. I thought it could be a career-ending type of thing, a season-ending thing.

"When I found out it would be a couple of months or whatever, I was pretty happy that was the case. It has been getting better and stronger every day, we're working through it.''

Barkov, whom Maurice said would be out another three weeks, did not have a timeline but said he was glad to be going through the rehab experience with Marchand.

"Hopefully, soon, both of us will be back,'' Barkov said. "It has been great to share the experience with Marchy, see what he does, how he gets ready."

Barkov was quick to point out Marchand was Enemy No. 1 back in his Bruins days.

"I like getting to know him better,'' Barkov said. "I didn't think I would ever say that.''

articles.title: Jaguars' Chris Rodriguez says offense got 'lax' with huddle timing
articles.summary: Jaguars RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. says Liam Coen addressed the offense's slow huddles as Jacksonville prepares for a loud road game against Baltimore.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have worked to clean up their offensive execution throughout the 2026 season, and running back Chris Rodriguez acknowledged that the team needed a reminder about one particularly important detail: getting in and out of the huddle quickly.

Speaking with reporters ahead of Thursday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens , Rodriguez was asked about the importance of getting back into the huddle promptly, particularly when crowd noise makes communication difficult.

"That's just us as an offense from the start," Rodriguez said in a video shared by Action Sports Jax . "We kind of got lax there at the beginning of the year, and coach kind of told us about it."

According to Rodriguez, head coach Liam Coen emphasized the need for players to get into the huddle and break it more quickly. The running back added that those expectations began during practice and are now being reinforced in team meetings.

Penalties are an issue that have been costly for Jacksonville.

During the Jaguars ' Week 5 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles in London, the offense committed three delay-of-game penalties, including two during a fourth-quarter possession that reached the Eagles' 1-yard line but ultimately ended without points.

Coen took responsibility for the problems afterward, acknowledging that his play calls sometimes included too much information for the offense to communicate quickly, and explained that simplifying calls could help players get lined up sooner, especially in loud environments.

Quarterback Trevor Lawrence also addressed the issue , explaining that ideally, the Jaguars would break the huddle with approximately 20 seconds remaining on the play clock. That would give the offense more time to identify defensive alignments, make adjustments, and prepare for the snap.

The Jaguars have shown improvement with penalties in recent weeks, including fewer delay-of-game flags. However, that could be challenging Thursday, as the Jaguars travel to Baltimore on a short week. M&T Bank Stadium is a notoriously difficult road environment, and communication becomes particularly important when crowd noise makes it harder for players to hear play calls and adjustments.

For Rodriguez and the rest of Jacksonville's offense, the preparation begins well before kickoff. And with the Jaguars looking to improve to 6-2, avoiding the communication problems that plagued them earlier this season could be an important part of securing their next victory.

It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride" or "sit Tommy DeVito." Instead, I search for players that could be perceived as fringe that could propel your lineups for weekly wins.

As always, if you have any questions or don't see your players here, feel free to follow me on Twitter (X) – @JamesNewell96 and send me a message, where I typically respond in a timely manner.

Jonah Coleman @ CAR (Projected FPTS – 14.4): Posting a 20.4-fantasy-point performance against the Chiefs, Coleman has successfully established himself as the Broncos' RB1. He played 66 percent of the snaps, had 15 total touches and played 27 more snaps than fellow back J.K. Dobbins. In the three games he's played, Coleman has averaged 10 carries, 77 total yards and 14.7 fantasy points. This week he goes against the Panthers, who are a supreme matchup for the rookie. Carolina has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game and 20 points per game to opposing RBs since Week Four. Coleman is a must-start and has the potential to hit RB1 numbers.

He has recorded at least 12 fantasy points in four of his last five games, including last Sunday against the Dolphins. The Patriots have the Packers next on their schedule in what is an RB-friendly matchup. Green Bay's defense has allowed 17-plus fantasy points to four backs this season. The Packers have also allowed the second-most rushing touchdowns and the fifth-most fantasy points per game to the position. Expect Stevenson to reach double-digit points this week.

Chase Brown vs. ATL (Projected FPTS – 15.8): Brown has not been the running back fantasy managers have been waiting for since drafting him in the first two rounds. He has scored fewer than 11 fantasy points in four games and has averaged 12.9 points per game this season. Brown is still managing a high snap count and has been close to finding the end zone, including last week, when he crossed the plane but the play was called back. I believe this will be the week Brown finally has his bounce-back game against the Falcons in Madrid. Atlanta's defense has allowed 21-plus fantasy points to five opposing running backs and has surrendered the third-most points to the position.

He enters Week Nine coming off his worst performance since becoming the lead back in Miami. Gordon has another tough matchup against the Lions, who pride themselves on stopping the run. Detroit's defense has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs. Since Gordon is not featured as a receiver, I don't imagine him getting a lot of work in a contest that will likely have Miami chasing points against a firepower offense.

Over the last three games without Lamar Jackson, Henry has averaged an uninspiring 8.3 fantasy points, 56.3 total yards per game and 3.5 yards per carry. He has scored only one touchdown and has one fumble. The Ravens will also be without Tyler Huntley in Week Nine against the Jaguars, who've allowed the fewest rushing yards per game and the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs. Henry has faced a loaded box on 46.7 percent of his carries over his previous three games, and Jacksonville should continue that strategy to stop him and force Baltimore to beat them with the arm of Joe Fagnano. Consider this a warning to Henry managers.

Saquon Barkley @ NYG (Projected FPTS – 13.6): I know, another big-name running back landing on my sit list in one week. Over the last two games since his return, Barkley has played a total of 32 snaps and has been on the field for 24 percent of the Eagles' offensive plays. I wouldn't be surprised if Barkley ends up scoring a touchdown inside the red zone, but it's hard to imagine how big his workload will be. Until he can resume his normal snap count or at least finish a game without an injury flare-up, I would avoid starting Barkley, even if it's a revenge game against his former team.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor trade: Indianapolis Colts running back's wife says process is 'driving me crazy'
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor's wife is on pins and needles as the Indianapolis Colts field offers for the running back.
articles.body:
Will Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor play this weekend? How many carries will he get? Will the Colts trade him?

Colts fans have been pondering those questions for a few weeks now. Imagine how Ayanna Taylor feels.

The running back's wife, who has been discussing the process on social media, said this week: "This waiting game is driving me crazy. I feel like a prized calf waiting for the slaughter. Is going to happen today? Tomorrow? Is it never gonna happen? And I genuinely cannot decide what's worse: being blindsided and sent away or being the last one standing, knowing what may be coming for you."

Jonathan Taylor could be one of the big prizes for a contending team at the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline . The Colts have been fielding offers for the 27-year-old seventh-year player.

See Colts RB Jonathan Taylor through the years

"You ever have the feeling that your entire life might change, but you just don't know when?" Ayanna Taylor said. "Well, welcome to my week, because that last game versus Jacksonville (a 42-7 loss) was rough. I've seen a lot of wins, I've seen a lot of losses over the years, but nothing quite like that. And now what are we supposed to do? Just wait?"

A few days remain before Jonathan Taylor's short-term fate is known, and Ayanna Taylor remains anxious.

"Something tells me we're not quite done with this chapter yet," she said.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani, Max Muncy up for Silver Slugger Awards
articles.summary: A pair of Dodgers are in the mix for a Silver Slugger Award in 2026. Max Muncy and Shohei Ohtani are one of two finalists at third base and designated hitter...
articles.body:
A pair of Dodgers are in the mix for a Silver Slugger Award in 2026. Max Muncy and Shohei Ohtani are one of two finalists at third base and designated hitter, respectively, in the National League, announced on Thursday morning.

Silver Slugger Awards, given annually to the top offensive players at each position in each league, are voted on by managers and three coaches from each team in their respective leagues.

Ohtani led National League designated hitters in on-base percentage (.377), OPS (.889), wRC+ (139), doubles (26) and stolen bases (11). Despite not hitting a home run after August 18 as he battled left knee and right biceps injuries, Ohtani's 30 home runs still ranked second among National League DHs.

Ohtani started 134 games as designated hitter, and was one of only four NL players to start at least 100 games at DH this season, along with Kyle Schwarber of the Philadelphia Phillies (147 starts), Iván Herrera of the St. Louis Cardinals (108), and Christian Yelich of the Milwaukee Brewers (106).

Schwarber is the other NL DH in the top two in voting for a Silver Slugger Award. Schwarber tied for the major league lead with 45 home runs and hit .232/.354/.503 with a 130 wRC+, 20 doubles, 105 walks, 97 RBI, and 95 runs scored.

Ohtani has four Silver Sluggers on his mantel, including 2024 and 2025 with the Dodgers in addition to 2021 and 2023 with the Angels. He was also a "finalist" at designated hitter in 2022 as well.

Muncy played in a career-high 149 games this season after two seasons with long stints on the injured list. He led all NL third baseman in OPS (.837), slugging percentage (.490), and wRC+ (129), hitting .252/.348/.490 with 29 home runs and a career-best 27 doubles.

Alex Bregman of the Chicago Cubs is the other NL third baseman in the top two of voting for a Silver Slugger Award. He hit .265/.355/.464 with a 128 wRC+, 28 home runs, 33 doubles, and 76 walks.

Muncy has not won a Silver Slugger Award, but he was among the top three in voting both in 2021 as a first baseman and in 2025 at third base despite playing in only 100 games.

Silver Slugger Awards have been around since 1980, and the only Dodgers third baseman to win one was Adrian Beltré in 2004.

Silver Slugger Award winners will be announced on Tuesday, November 17.
